violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: COOKED POTATOES (119) IN THE 1-DOOR UPRIGHT HH UNIT FOR 1 HOUR. TEMPERATURE OF THE UNIT READ 130 F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. CDI: PIC INCREASED THE TEMPERATURE OF THE UNIT. PIC WILL DISCARD THE POTATOES IN TWO HOURS.

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: PACKAGED FROZEN RAW LAMB THAWING ON THE PREP TABLE.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. CDI: PIC PLACED THE PACKAGED LAMB UNDER COLD RUNNING WATER.

violations.title: Insect Control Devices, Installation
violations.observation: Insect control device is located on the wall over single use articles where dead insects may be impelled or fall.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. OBSERVED CONTAINERS OF DRY GOODS AND CONTAINER OF DOUGH STORED ON THE FLOOR.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. ENSURE ALL FOODS ARE KEPT OFF THE FLOOR.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: cooked onions were being held at room temperature and were 66ºF. Cooked onions must be held hot or cold and not at room temperature.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. The onions were out of temperature for 3 hours. The PIC was advised to serve the onions in the next hour or discard them. The PIC requested to use TPHC for cooked onions moving forward. A TPHC policy for cooked onions was created during the inspection and entered into the record. Be sure to properly label each batch of onions to show when they were removed from temperature control. CDI.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: There was an unlabeled spray bottle with pink liquid in it at the bus station cart.
violations.corrective_action: The spray bottle contained quaternary ammonia solution for cleaning tables. Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: a 12 quart container full of cooked lentils was placed in the walk-in refrigerator directly from the stove to cool. Also, a coveredcontainer of cooked beef broth that was 108° was placed in the walk-in too cool.
violations.corrective_action: Placing large amounts of food in large containers and in the walk-in while still hot will not allow the food to cool down rapidly. The food should be broken up into smaller pans and uncovered in order to cool properly. Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. The EHS discussed this with the PIC. CDI.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: ice scoop handles were stored in the ice; rice scoop handles were stored in the hot rice; flour handle was stored in the flour.
violations.corrective_action: Scoops can be stored in foods, but the scoop handles must be stored out of the food to prevent bare hand contact with foods. Discontinue storing scoop handles in foods as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items, Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: A case of single service cups and lids were stored on the floor under the counter behind the front counter.
violations.corrective_action: Discontinue storing food equipment on the floor. Store all food equipment (and food) at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. Observed one employee handling raw chicken with gloved hands and then pick up cooked falafel and serve it. Observed another employee was washing dirty equipment with gloved hands, then proceeded to roll out bread dough and touch baked bread.
violations.corrective_action: In both instances, the employees should have taken off their gloves and washed their hands between their tasks. ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. The environmental health specialist (EHS) spoke with both employees about this and had them wash their hands immediately.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: Raw chicken was stored over beef liver in the walk- in.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). The person in charge (PIC) moved the chicken to the lower shelf.

violations.title: Chemical Sanitizing, Contact Time Met
violations.observation: The food employee did not immerse a large cambro container while washing and sanitizing.
violations.corrective_action: Chemical sanitization (manual or mechanical operations) including the application of sanitizing chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods using a solution by providing: 1) an exposure time of at least 10 seconds for a chlorine solution, 2) an exposure time of at least 7 seconds for a chlorine solution of 50mg/L that has a pH of 10 or less and a water temperature of 100F or a pH of 8 or less and a water temperature of 75F, 3) an exposure time of at least 30 seconds for other chemical sanitizing solutions, or 4) an exposure time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and pH that when evaluated for efficacy yields sanitization. The EHS explained the requirement to the food employee and demonstrated that equipment must be fully immersed for at least 30 seconds. FAVA POT (Inspection Date: 10/16/2025) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: cooked potatoes in the hot holding cabinet were 118F. The hot holding cabinet was set to 98F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. The PIC reheated the potatoes in the oven to correct.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter. Observed several wet wiping cloths stored on counters and food prep tables.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: observed scoops with handles used to dispense foods and ingredients, but the handles were in the food. Observed bowls being used to scoop foods and ingredients.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently.

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: The cold water faucet handle on the food prep sink does not work.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. Repair the cold water faucet handles within 6 months.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' EHP documentation was not available.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. EHS provided a copy of the documentation.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events. EHS observed no bodily fluids cleanup procedure
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.
